clue.text: Danger! Noun penned by this compiler genius

indicators.note: a letter penned by others is enclosed by them, as if fenced in a pen

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so this compiler is ME
an ace is an expert, someone of genius at a skill
N is the grammar abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of their brilliance while warning of danger in a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat or source of peril, a synonym for danger.

clue.text: Central heating in 22 busted? One'll fix it

indicators.note: the heating abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
busted means broken, so the letters of 22 are rearranged

parts.note: 22 refers to the answer at 22 across, meaning movies

explanation.surface: The heating at the picture house has broken; someone will repair it.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 22 means its answer is the anagram fodder; 'busted' makes MEANIC from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic is a tradesperson who repairs engines and machinery.

clue.text: VIP old boy under arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue the old boy sits below the word for arrest

parts.note: to nab is to arrest
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A distinguished former pupil is taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a wealthy, important person, originally a Mughal governor.

clue.text: Fortune left section of church

parts.note: chance is luck or fortune

explanation.surface: Luck has deserted part of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area round the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Damage reputation of space station in school

indicators.note: the space station sits inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station

explanation.surface: Someone smears the good name of a space station within a school setting.
explanation.walkthrough: To smirch is an old verb meaning to stain or sully, mostly met now in 'besmirch'.
explanation.definitionFit: To smirch someone is to sully or tarnish their good name, so it damages standing.

clue.text: Drink one needs to get over bird? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down clue getting over means placed above, one on top of the bird
on the contrary reverses the order, so the bird goes above the one

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cocktail that helps a person recover from a lost love.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue first puts I above MARTIN; 'On the contrary' flips that, so MARTIN comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Theatre company feel bad about show

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
to resent something is to feel bitter about it

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors is unhappy about a production.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent can mean to depict or portray, to show.

clue.text: Charioteeer, ejecting Ben, was ahead of cast

indicators.note: ejecting means throwing out, so the first name is removed

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the chariot racer in the novel and film
Ben is taken as written
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A chariot racer throws someone out in front of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors in the film, but it means threw.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurled means threw with force, flung, in the past tense like cast.

clue.text: Dull system of bank payments returned cover

indicators.note: returned means the two words together are read backwards

parts.note: drab means dull or colourless
BACS is the UK automated clearing system that moves payments between banks

explanation.surface: A dreary banking transfer system comes back with some protective cover.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the British interbank system that handles direct debits and salary payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath that covers and protects a sword blade.

clue.text: Former Chancellor making headline? Yes

indicators.note: making here means forming something new out of the letters

explanation.surface: Is an ex-Chancellor of the Exchequer getting into the news? Yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Denis Healey was Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, the finance minister, from 1974 to 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour politician served as Chancellor of the Exchequer in the Wilson and Callaghan governments.

clue.text: Engineers drink pop

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Army engineers knock back a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like a fizzy drink, but here it is a bang, a sharp sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp explosive sound of a gun firing, a bang or pop.

clue.text: Boast about clothes

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for boast is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about their wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially a distinctive style of dress or outfit.

clue.text: Support a ventricle that's shaky

indicators.note: something shaky is unsteady and wobbles, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical note: support a heart chamber that's failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' sounds medical alongside the heart chamber, but it is the definition: a structural bracket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam fixed at one end that holds up a balcony or bridge span.

clue.text: US president's pay for working in area around Boston

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth US president; the possessive gives the S
hire is the wages paid for labour, as in 'the labourer is worthy of his hire'

explanation.surface: An American president's salary while working near Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: Boston points to Massachusetts, but this is the original Boston, a port town in the English county of Lincolnshire on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county contains the market town of Boston, so it is the region surrounding it.

clue.text: Two coppers meeting topless smouldering things — they could be pickled

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the second of the two copper symbols

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is dropped in this down clue

parts.note: embers are glowing remnants of a fire

explanation.surface: Two police officers find some smouldering items that might be preserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' hints at drunks, but these are vegetables preserved in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gherkins and other small cucumbers are commonly preserved in brine or vinegar.

clue.text: Bliss perhaps of calm river

parts.note: to compose oneself is to calm down

explanation.surface: Peaceful joy found beside a tranquil river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bliss' looks like happiness, but is Sir Arthur Bliss, the English composer and Master of the Queen's Music.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss wrote music, so he is an example of a writer of scores.

clue.text: King's mistress engaged in making battlement

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside, held within the word for making

parts.note: creation is the act of making something
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A royal mistress busies herself constructing castle defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A crenellation is the notched parapet on top of a castle wall, with gaps for archers.

clue.text: Hour in space is unable to delight

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em

indicators.note: the hour goes inside the combined letters

parts.note: can't means is unable

explanation.surface: Someone stuck for an hour in space cannot be pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to charm or captivate, filling someone with delight.

clue.text: Temptation to consume drug is for relaxation

indicators.note: to consume means to take in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or temptation
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The temptation to take drugs to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent at ease, rest and recreation.

clue.text: Draw of Queen appearing in disreputable club

indicators.note: the queen's letters appear inside the club

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A sketch of the monarch turning up in a seedy nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a picture, but here it means obtain or extract.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to obtain it from a source, as one draws comfort from it.

clue.text: Pasta poor church creatures fed to sick clergyman coming round

indicators.note: fed to means the creatures go inside, as food goes into a mouth
coming round means the sick clergyman is read backwards

parts.note: ill means sick
Rev is short for Reverend, a member of the clergy
'poor as a church mouse' is a proverb, so the church creatures are mice

explanation.surface: Pasta is served to an ailing vicar's mice as he recovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' turns ILLREV into VERLLI, which is split by MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermicelli is a very thin noodle, a type of Italian pasta.

clue.text: Stupid person to perform exercise

parts.note: to do something is to perform it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone foolish going through an exercise routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: A number enjoy computer stuff

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Someone who likes working with computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral from zero to nine is called a digit.

clue.text: Movies showing spies framing soldiers from the East

indicators.note: the spies surround the soldiers, like a frame around a picture

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the East means read right to left

parts.note: men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A film show featuring spies hemming in soldiers from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema means the film industry or films collectively, the movies.

clue.text: Yard with dilapidated housing, not that old

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A yard with run-down housing that is still fairly recent.
explanation.definitionFit: Youngish means fairly young, so someone not especially old.

clue.text: Dealers at Zurich concealing fake

indicators.note: the words conceal the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: Swiss bankers hiding a counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, so something not genuine.

clue.text: Gambler improved

definitions.meaning: one who bets or places wagers
made or become superior, comparative of good

explanation.surface: A gambler who has got better at it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who bets is a punter; and the comparative of good means improved.
